Driver Wellbeing

Driver wellbeing to take centre stage at UK Bus Summit 2026

September 10, 2026 Mark Salisbury Filed under: Bus News, Busworld Europe, Driver Safety, Driver Wellbeing, Fleet Management, News, Newsletter, Top News
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:52
Instaread

Driver safety and wellbeing are set to dominate discussions as senior figures from government, transport authorities and the bus industry gather for the UK Bus Summit 2026 on 10 September. Among the topics shaping the sector’s direction is Transport for London’s Bus Safety Standard 2 (BSS2), which places fresh emphasis on the driver’s working environment. Pailton Engineering has spent years exploring these principles, developing an ergonomic driver pod that shows how greater adjustability could improve comfort and wellbeing behind the wheel.

The summit takes place at The Spine in Liverpool and brings together a high-profile speaker line-up, including Simon Lightwood MP, Minister for Roads and Buses; Steve Rotheram, Mayor of Liverpool City Region; Oliver Coppard, Mayor of South Yorkshire; Leon Daniels OBE, Chair of the Bus Centre of Excellence Advisory Board; and Jason Prince, Director of the Urban Transport Group.

With BSS2 expected to influence bus procurement from 2029 onwards, the event offers an important platform for discussing how safety, accessibility and driver welfare will shape the next generation of buses. As operators and manufacturers look ahead to these new standards, the driver’s cab is increasingly viewed not just as a workspace but as a key factor in recruitment, retention and long-term health outcomes across the industry.

Pailton Engineering’s driver pod was built to put these principles into practice. Developed over several years, it pairs a fully electric tilting head steering column with a realistic bus workstation, giving operators, manufacturers and authorities the chance to experience firsthand how improved adjustability can suit drivers of different heights and body types.

The concept grew out of the company’s work on a new electric steering column, first unveiled as a prototype at Busworld 2019, and refined in the years since in response to feedback from across the industry. By Busworld 2025, Pailton had integrated the technology into a fully functioning driver pod complete with electronic memory settings, allowing drivers to recall their preferred driving position at the touch of a button.

“The conversation around bus safety is recognising that protecting drivers is just as important as protecting passengers,” said Roger Brereton, Head of Sales at Pailton Engineering. “When we began developing the driver pod, we wanted to show that relatively simple ergonomic improvements could make the driving position more comfortable for a much wider range of people.

“With BSS2 now placing greater emphasis on personalisation and adjustability, it’s encouraging to see many of those same principles becoming part of the industry’s future direction. Better ergonomics can help reduce musculoskeletal strain, improve the driver experience and ultimately support operators tackling recruitment and retention challenges.”

The driver pod remains available for demonstrations at Pailton Engineering’s Coventry headquarters, giving manufacturers, operators and transport authorities the opportunity to experience its ergonomic features firsthand ahead of the standards taking effect.
